title: Telling a Research Story
editorial_note: Opening revised to lead with the lesson itself. Remaining dialogue is an automated editorial draft; review spoken wording and meaning before final publication.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Telling a Research Story.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Research storytelling structures evidence so an audience can understand why it matters and what to do next. Start with the decision or tension, introduce the person and context, show representative evidence, explain the insight and confidence, then state the implication. Use stories to clarify, not manipulate.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why does that happen?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Tailor detail to the audience while preserving traceability and uncertainty. Executives may need decision implications; engineers may need edge cases and constraints; designers may need behavioural detail. The underlying evidence should remain available.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Build narrative from evidence and choice
turns.text: What changes when we look at build narrative from evidence and choice?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Different audiences need different depth, but the evidence remains traceable. Leaders see consequence and decision; delivery teams see behaviours and edge cases; operations see handoffs and capacity. Uncertainty, counter-evidence, and people who do not fit the dominant story remain visible.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The close names the decision, recommended next test, owner, and what would change the conclusion.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Storyboard the reasoning, not just the drama
turns.text: What changes when we look at storyboard the reasoning, not just the drama?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Numbers establish reach only when denominator and population match. A quote supplies meaning only with context. A blueprint explains system cause but does not estimate frequency. The presenter says which role each piece plays so stakeholders do not treat all visual evidence as interchangeable proof.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: After the playback, the owner records a decision, unresolved objection, action, and review trigger. If stakeholders remember only the dramatic patient and cannot state the mechanism or choice, the story has created sympathy without shared product judgment.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at structure for a decision?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Begin with the audience, decision, stakes, and what they already know. Establish the person and context, show the evidence pattern, explain the mechanism, connect it to consequence, and present choices or next learning. Use selected stories to make a pattern concrete while preserving its limits.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Distinguish evidence, interpretation, and recommendation visually and verbally. Include counterevidence, uncertainty, sample and method limits, and source traceability. Quantitative scale and qualitative mechanism strengthen one another when their populations and definitions align.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Tailor depth without changing truth. Leaders may need consequence and decision; delivery teams need scenarios and evidence; operational teams need handoffs and ownership. Provide access to supporting material. A persuasive story must not become advocacy that hides inconvenient evidence.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Build an evidence spine that survives retelling
turns.text: What changes when we look at build an evidence spine that survives retelling?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The story also makes alternatives legible. An interface-only confirmation is faster and cheaper but may mask disagreement. A durable receipt improves inspectability but still needs authoritative updates. Reconciliation monitoring adds operational cost while addressing the underlying failure.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Leadership is asked to choose the level of intervention and risk, not simply approve the research team's preferred screen.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Persuasion without calibrated confidence is advocacy theatre. State what is known, what is inferred, what remains uncertain, and what decision is justified now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should we look at more closely?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A strong evidence story makes its reasoning inspectable. Begin with the decision and why it matters. Place the audience in a representative context, show a small amount of direct evidence, explain the pattern and its confidence, then name the implication and unanswered questions.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: This structure gives a team enough human detail to care without allowing a single story to substitute for the whole evidence base.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Match form to purpose. A short playback may create shared context; a one-page decision brief can clarify action; a working session may help teams interpret evidence together; a repository preserves traceability for later use. Present uncertainty honestly. When evidence is early, say what would strengthen or challenge it rather than performing certainty to win approval.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Failure modes to watch

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Emotional manipulation: an exceptional story is used to force a predetermined decision. Evidence-free conclusion: the recommendation arrives without an inspectable chain. Audience mismatch: detailed research is delivered where a decision needs clear implications, or vice versa. No follow-through: a compelling presentation ends without owner, next test, or decision.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A dramatic quote can win attention but distort prevalence. Pairing one representative episode with distribution, exceptions, and source links creates a story that is memorable without becoming manipulation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does this connect to what we have already learned?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Synthesis creates patterns, personas, scenarios, and maps. This lesson turns them into influence. Module 7 applies the same clarity to information, language, navigation, and findability.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Explain one insight as a short story without exaggerating its certainty. Include the audience, context, evidence, implication, and limitation.
